To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hybridity in regulation is a concept that can be used to understand the complexity of the global political economy.

the concept of hybrid regulation is a useful way of understanding the complexity of the global political economy, and that it is particularly useful for understanding the role of the State and the emergence of new forms of authority in the context of the global economy.
the hybridization of regulation is a process that is taking place on different levels of the global political economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of new forms of hybridity in the global political economy.
the emergence of new hybrid forms of regulation, the hybrid nature of subjects, and hybrid forms of space.
the following questions: What are the new subjects and objects of hybrid regulation in the global political economy and what is their impact on the state?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hybridity, in its multiple forms, is the new normality of the global political economy, and that it is the main characteristic of the global political economic system of our time.
global hybrids are not just a matter of new regulatory forms, but also of the subjects involved, the objects regulated and the spaces where regulation takes place.
the concept of hybrid is a useful analytical tool for understanding the new forms of governance in the global political economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hybridisation of regulatory practices is a key element in the understanding of contemporary globalisation.
the paper provides a new approach to the analysis of the hybridity of regulation in the global political economy.

the notion of global hybrid regulation provides an analytical framework that can help to overcome the limitations of both the regulation approach and the international political economy perspective in understanding the dynamics of globalisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
regulation theory can be enriched by the critical international political economy approach.
regulation theory can benefit from a more explicit focus on transnational hybrid forms of regulation.
regulation is not just a process of negotiation among social actors.
